True Statement: Endocrine glands lack ducts and hence are called ductless glands.
False 1: Exocrine glands lack ducts and hence are called ductless glands.

True Statement: Hormones are non-nutrient chemicals which act as intercellular messengers and are produced in trace amounts.
False 1: Hormones are non-nutrient chemicals which act as intercellular messengers and are produced in large amounts.
False 2: Hormones are nutrient chemicals which act as intercellular messengers and are produced in trace amounts.

True Statement: Organised endocrine bodies include pituitary, pineal, thyroid, adrenal, pancreas, parathyroid, thymus and gonads.
False 1: Organised endocrine bodies include pituitary, pineal, thyroid, adrenal, pancreas, parathyroid, thymus and liver.

True Statement: In addition to organised endocrine glands, the gastrointestinal tract, liver, kidney and heart also produce hormones.
False 1: In addition to organised endocrine glands, the gastrointestinal tract, spleen, kidney and heart also produce hormones.

True Statement: The hypothalamus is the basal part of diencephalon, forebrain.
False 1: The hypothalamus is the basal part of the cerebrum, forebrain.
False 2: The hypothalamus is the dorsal part of diencephalon, forebrain.

True Statement: The hypothalamus contains neurosecretory cells called nuclei which produce hormones that regulate the synthesis and secretion of pituitary hormones.
False 1: The pineal gland contains neurosecretory cells called nuclei which produce hormones that regulate pituitary hormone synthesis and secretion.

True Statement: Hypothalamic releasing hormones stimulate secretion of pituitary hormones; inhibiting hormones inhibit secretion of pituitary hormones.
False 1: Hypothalamic releasing hormones inhibit secretion of pituitary hormones; inhibiting hormones stimulate secretion of pituitary hormones.

True Statement: Gonadotrophin releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulates pituitary synthesis and release of gonadotrophins.
False 1: Gonadotrophin releasing hormone (GnRH) inhibits pituitary synthesis and release of gonadotrophins.
False 2: Somatostatin stimulates pituitary synthesis and release of gonadotrophins.

True Statement: Somatostatin from the hypothalamus inhibits the release of growth hormone from the pituitary.
False 1: Somatostatin from the hypothalamus stimulates the release of growth hormone from the pituitary.
False 2: GnRH inhibits the release of growth hormone from the pituitary.

True Statement: Hypothalamic hormones reach the pituitary gland through a portal circulatory system and regulate the functions of the anterior pituitary.
False 1: Hypothalamic hormones reach the pituitary gland through the lymphatic system and regulate the functions of the anterior pituitary.
False 2: Hypothalamic hormones reach the pituitary gland through a portal circulatory system and regulate the functions of the posterior pituitary.

True Statement: The posterior pituitary is under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus.
False 1: The anterior pituitary is under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus.
False 2: The pineal gland is under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus.

True Statement: The pituitary gland is located in a bony cavity called sella tursica and is attached to the hypothalamus by a stalk.
False 1: The pituitary gland is located in a bony cavity called sella tursica and is attached to the thalamus by a stalk.

True Statement: Pituitary is divided into adenohypophysis (pars distalis and pars intermedia) and neurohypophysis (pars nervosa = posterior pituitary).
False 1: Neurohypophysis consists of pars distalis and pars intermedia; adenohypophysis is pars nervosa.
False 2: Adenohypophysis includes pars nervosa; neurohypophysis includes pars distalis.

True Statement: Pars distalis (anterior pituitary) produces GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH.
False 1: Pars intermedia produces GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH.
False 2: Pars distalis produces only MSH.

True Statement: Pars intermedia secretes only one hormone — melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH).
False 1: Pars distalis secretes only MSH.
False 2: Pars nervosa (neurohypophysis) secretes only MSH.

True Statement: Neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary) stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin, which are actually synthesised by the hypothalamus.
False 1: Adenohypophysis (anterior pituitary) stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin synthesised by the hypothalamus.
False 2: Neurohypophysis stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin, which are synthesised by the anterior pituitary.

True Statement: Over-secretion of GH causes gigantism; low secretion of GH causes pituitary dwarfism.
False 1: Low secretion of GH causes gigantism; over-secretion of GH causes pituitary dwarfism.

True Statement: Excess secretion of GH in adults (especially middle age) results in acromegaly — severe disfigurement especially of the face.
False 1: Excess secretion of prolactin in adults results in acromegaly.
False 2: Excess secretion of GH in adults results in gigantism.

True Statement: Prolactin regulates the growth of the mammary glands and formation of milk in them.
False 1: Oxytocin regulates the growth of the mammary glands and formation of milk in them.
False 2: TSH regulates the growth of the mammary glands and formation of milk in them.

True Statement: TSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones from the thyroid gland.
False 1: ACTH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones from the thyroid gland.
False 2: TSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex.

True Statement: ACTH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex.
False 1: TSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex.
False 2: ACTH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones from the thyroid gland.

True Statement: LH and FSH stimulate gonadal activity and hence are called gonadotrophins.
False 1: TSH and ACTH stimulate gonadal activity and hence are called gonadotrophins.
False 2: LH and FSH stimulate thyroid activity and hence are called gonadotrophins.

True Statement: In males, LH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of androgens from the testis.
False 1: In males, FSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of androgens from the testis.
False 2: In males, LH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of glucocorticoids from the testis.

True Statement: In males, FSH and androgens together regulate spermatogenesis.
False 1: In males, LH and androgens together regulate spermatogenesis.
False 2: In males, FSH and estrogens together regulate spermatogenesis.

True Statement: In females, LH induces ovulation of fully mature graafian follicles and maintains the corpus luteum.
False 1: In females, FSH induces ovulation of fully mature graafian follicles and maintains the corpus luteum.
False 2: In females, LH stimulates the growth and development of ovarian follicles.

True Statement: FSH stimulates growth and development of the ovarian follicles in females.
False 1: LH stimulates growth and development of the ovarian follicles in females.
False 2: ACTH stimulates growth and development of the ovarian follicles in females.

True Statement: MSH acts on melanocytes (melanin-containing cells) and regulates pigmentation of the skin.
False 1: TSH acts on melanocytes and regulates pigmentation of the skin.
False 2: MSH acts on the adrenal cortex and regulates pigmentation of the skin.

True Statement: Oxytocin acts on smooth muscles and stimulates their contraction; in females, it stimulates vigorous contraction of the uterus at childbirth and milk ejection from the mammary gland.
False 1: Vasopressin acts on smooth muscles and stimulates their contraction; in females, it stimulates uterus contraction and milk ejection.
False 2: Oxytocin acts on smooth muscles; in females, it stimulates formation of milk (not milk ejection) from the mammary gland.

True Statement: Vasopressin (ADH) acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates resorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules, reducing loss of water through urine.
False 1: Oxytocin acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates resorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules.
False 2: Vasopressin (ADH) acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates loss of water through urine.

True Statement: Impairment affecting synthesis or release of ADH results in water loss and dehydration — a condition called Diabetes Insipidus.
False 1: Impairment affecting synthesis or release of insulin results in water loss and dehydration — a condition called Diabetes Insipidus.
False 2: Impairment affecting synthesis or release of ADH results in Diabetes Mellitus.

True Statement: The pineal gland is located on the dorsal side of the forebrain.
False 1: The pineal gland is located on the ventral side of the forebrain.
False 2: The pineal gland is located on the dorsal side of the midbrain.

True Statement: Pineal secretes melatonin, which plays a very important role in the regulation of a 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of the body, including the sleep-wake cycle and body temperature.
False 1: Pineal secretes thymosins, which play an important role in the regulation of the 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of the body.
False 2: Melatonin regulates blood calcium levels.

True Statement: Melatonin also influences metabolism, pigmentation, the menstrual cycle and defense capability.
False 1: Vasopressin influences metabolism, pigmentation, the menstrual cycle and defense capability.

True Statement: The thyroid gland has two lobes located on either side of the trachea, interconnected by a thin flap of connective tissue called isthmus.
False 1: The thyroid gland has two lobes located on either side of the oesophagus, interconnected by isthmus.
False 2: The thyroid gland has two lobes interconnected by the corpus callosum.

True Statement: Thyroid follicular cells synthesise two hormones: tetraiodothyronine (T₄/thyroxine) and triiodothyronine (T₃).
False 1: Parathyroid cells synthesise T₄ and T₃.
False 2: Thyroid follicular cells synthesise PTH and TCT.

True Statement: Iodine is essential for the normal rate of hormone synthesis in the thyroid.
False 1: Calcium is essential for the normal rate of hormone synthesis in the thyroid.
False 2: Iodine is essential for the normal rate of insulin synthesis in the pancreas.

True Statement: Deficiency of iodine results in hypothyroidism and enlargement of the thyroid gland (goitre).
False 1: Excess iodine results in hypothyroidism and enlargement of the thyroid gland (goitre).
False 2: Deficiency of iodine results in hyperthyroidism and enlargement of the thyroid gland.

True Statement: Hypothyroidism during pregnancy causes cretinism — stunted growth, mental retardation, low IQ, abnormal skin, deaf-mutism.
False 1: Hyperthyroidism during pregnancy causes cretinism.
False 2: Hypothyroidism during pregnancy causes acromegaly.

True Statement: Hypothyroidism in adult women may cause the menstrual cycle to become irregular.
False 1: Hyperthyroidism in adult women may cause the menstrual cycle to become irregular.

True Statement: Exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease) is a form of hyperthyroidism characterised by thyroid enlargement, protrusion of eyeballs, increased BMR and weight loss.
False 1: Exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease) is a form of hypothyroidism characterised by thyroid enlargement, protrusion of eyeballs, increased BMR and weight loss.
False 2: Exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease) is characterised by decreased BMR and weight gain.

True Statement: Thyroid hormones play an important role in regulating the basal metabolic rate and support the process of red blood cell formation.
False 1: Parathyroid hormones play an important role in regulating the basal metabolic rate.
False 2: Thyroid hormones play an important role in regulating blood calcium levels.

True Statement: Thyroid hormones control the metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins and fats, and influence maintenance of water and electrolyte balance.
False 1: Glucocorticoids control the metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins and fats, and influence maintenance of water and electrolyte balance.

True Statement: The thyroid gland also secretes a protein hormone called thyrocalcitonin (TCT) which regulates blood calcium levels.
False 1: The parathyroid gland secretes thyrocalcitonin (TCT) which regulates blood calcium levels.
False 2: The thyroid gland also secretes PTH which regulates blood calcium levels.

True Statement: In humans, four parathyroid glands are present on the back side of the thyroid gland, one pair each in the two lobes of the thyroid gland.
False 1: In humans, two parathyroid glands are present on the back side of the thyroid gland.
False 2: In humans, four parathyroid glands are present on the front side of the thyroid gland.

True Statement: The parathyroid glands secrete a peptide hormone called parathyroid hormone (PTH).
False 1: The thyroid gland secretes PTH.
False 2: The parathyroid glands secrete TCT.

True Statement: The secretion of PTH is regulated by the circulating levels of calcium ions.
False 1: The secretion of PTH is regulated by the circulating levels of glucose.
False 2: The secretion of TSH is regulated by the circulating levels of calcium ions.

True Statement: PTH is a hypercalcemic hormone — it increases blood Ca²⁺ by stimulating bone resorption, renal Ca²⁺ reabsorption and Ca²⁺ absorption from digested food.
False 1: PTH is a hypocalcemic hormone — it decreases blood Ca²⁺.
False 2: TCT is a hypercalcemic hormone that increases blood Ca²⁺.

True Statement: PTH and TCT together play a significant role in calcium balance in the body.
False 1: PTH and insulin together play a significant role in calcium balance in the body.
False 2: PTH alone maintains complete calcium balance in the body.

True Statement: The thymus gland is a lobular structure located between the lungs behind the sternum on the ventral side of the aorta.
False 1: The thymus gland is located between the lungs behind the sternum on the dorsal side of the aorta.
False 2: The thymus gland is located behind the trachea, in front of the sternum.

True Statement: Thymus secretes thymosins which play a major role in the differentiation of T-lymphocytes, providing cell-mediated immunity.
False 1: Thyroid secretes thymosins which differentiate T-lymphocytes, providing cell-mediated immunity.
False 2: Thymus secretes thymosins which differentiate B-lymphocytes, providing cell-mediated immunity.

True Statement: Thymosins also promote production of antibodies to provide humoral immunity.
False 1: Thymosins inhibit production of antibodies.
False 2: Estrogens promote production of antibodies to provide humoral immunity.

True Statement: Thymus degenerates in old individuals, resulting in decreased production of thymosins and weakened immune responses.
False 1: Thymus degenerates in young individuals, resulting in decreased production of thymosins.
False 2: Thymus degenerates in old individuals, resulting in increased production of thymosins.

True Statement: Each adrenal gland is located one above each kidney; it is composed of adrenal medulla (central) and adrenal cortex (outer).
False 1: Each adrenal gland is composed of adrenal medulla (outer) and adrenal cortex (central).
False 2: Each adrenal gland is located below each kidney.

True Statement: The adrenal medulla secretes two hormones — adrenaline (epinephrine) and noradrenaline (norepinephrine) — collectively called catecholamines.
False 1: The adrenal cortex secretes adrenaline (epinephrine) and noradrenaline (norepinephrine).
False 2: The adrenal medulla secretes cortisol and aldosterone.

True Statement: Adrenaline and noradrenaline are called emergency hormones or hormones of Fight or Flight.
False 1: Oxytocin and vasopressin are called emergency hormones or hormones of Fight or Flight.
False 2: Glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids are called emergency hormones or hormones of Fight or Flight.

True Statement: Catecholamines increase alertness, pupillary dilation, piloerection, sweating, heart beat, strength of heart contraction and rate of respiration.
False 1: Catecholamines decrease heart beat and rate of respiration.

True Statement: Catecholamines stimulate the breakdown of glycogen resulting in increased blood glucose, and also stimulate breakdown of lipids and proteins.
False 1: Catecholamines stimulate the synthesis of glycogen resulting in decreased blood glucose.
False 2: Catecholamines stimulate breakdown of glycogen resulting in decreased blood glucose.

True Statement: The adrenal cortex has three layers: zona reticularis (inner), zona fasciculata (middle) and zona glomerulosa (outer).
False 1: The adrenal cortex has three layers: zona reticularis (outer), zona fasciculata (middle) and zona glomerulosa (inner).
False 2: The adrenal cortex has three layers: zona fasciculata (inner), zona reticularis (middle) and zona glomerulosa (outer).

True Statement: Glucocorticoids are involved in carbohydrate metabolism (e.g., cortisol); mineralocorticoids regulate water and electrolyte balance (e.g., aldosterone).
False 1: Mineralocorticoids are involved in carbohydrate metabolism; glucocorticoids regulate water and electrolyte balance.

True Statement: Glucocorticoids (cortisol) stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis, and inhibit cellular uptake and utilisation of amino acids.
False 1: Glucocorticoids inhibit gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis.
False 2: Mineralocorticoids stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis.

True Statement: Cortisol produces anti-inflammatory reactions and suppresses the immune response; cortisol also stimulates RBC production.
False 1: Cortisol promotes inflammatory reactions.
False 2: Aldosterone produces anti-inflammatory reactions and suppresses the immune response.

True Statement: Aldosterone acts on the renal tubules and stimulates reabsorption of Na⁺ and water, and excretion of K⁺ and phosphate ions.
False 1: Cortisol acts on the renal tubules and stimulates reabsorption of Na⁺ and water, and excretion of K⁺.
False 2: Aldosterone stimulates excretion of Na⁺ and water, and reabsorption of K⁺ and phosphate ions.

True Statement: Small amounts of androgenic steroids secreted by the adrenal cortex play a role in growth of axial hair, pubic hair and facial hair during puberty.
False 1: Glucocorticoids secreted by the adrenal cortex play a role in growth of axial hair, pubic hair and facial hair during puberty.
False 2: Androgenic steroids secreted by the adrenal medulla play a role in hair growth during puberty.

True Statement: Underproduction of hormones by the adrenal cortex causes altered carbohydrate metabolism, acute weakness and fatigue — a condition called Addison's disease.
False 1: Overproduction of hormones by the adrenal cortex causes Addison's disease.
False 2: Underproduction of hormones by the adrenal medulla causes Addison's disease.

True Statement: There are about 1 to 2 million Islets of Langerhans in a normal human pancreas, representing 1 to 2 per cent of the pancreatic tissue.
False 1: There are about 1 to 2 million Islets of Langerhans representing 10 to 12 per cent of the pancreatic tissue.
False 2: There are about 1000 to 2000 Islets of Langerhans in a normal human pancreas.

True Statement: In the Islets of Langerhans, α-cells secrete glucagon and β-cells secrete insulin.
False 1: In the Islets of Langerhans, α-cells secrete insulin and β-cells secrete glucagon.

True Statement: Glucagon stimulates glycogenolysis in liver cells (hepatocytes) resulting in increased blood sugar (hyperglycemia).
False 1: Insulin stimulates glycogenolysis in liver cells resulting in increased blood sugar.
False 2: Glucagon stimulates glycogenolysis in liver cells resulting in decreased blood sugar (hypoglycemia).

True Statement: Glucagon stimulates gluconeogenesis and reduces cellular glucose uptake; hence it is called a hyperglycemic hormone.
False 1: Glucagon inhibits gluconeogenesis; hence it is called a hypoglycemic hormone.
False 2: Insulin stimulates gluconeogenesis and reduces cellular glucose uptake; hence it is called a hyperglycemic hormone.

True Statement: Insulin enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilisation in hepatocytes and adipocytes, resulting in decreased blood glucose levels (hypoglycemia).
False 1: Glucagon enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilisation resulting in hypoglycemia.
False 2: Insulin reduces cellular glucose uptake and utilisation, resulting in increased blood glucose levels (hyperglycemia).

True Statement: Insulin stimulates conversion of glucose to glycogen (glycogenesis) in target cells.
False 1: Glucagon stimulates conversion of glucose to glycogen (glycogenesis) in target cells.
False 2: Insulin stimulates conversion of glycogen to glucose (glycogenolysis) in target cells.

True Statement: Prolonged hyperglycemia leads to diabetes mellitus, which is associated with loss of glucose through urine and formation of ketone bodies.
False 1: Prolonged hypoglycemia leads to diabetes mellitus.
False 2: Prolonged hyperglycemia leads to Diabetes Insipidus.

True Statement: The testis is located in the scrotal sac (outside the abdomen).
False 1: The testis is located inside the abdomen.

True Statement: Leydig cells (interstitial cells) present in the intertubular spaces of the testis produce androgens, mainly testosterone.
False 1: Sertoli cells present in the intertubular spaces of the testis produce androgens, mainly testosterone.
False 2: Leydig cells produce estrogens, mainly estradiol.

True Statement: Androgens regulate the development, maturation and functions of the male accessory sex organs (epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicles, prostate gland, urethra).
False 1: Estrogens regulate the development, maturation and functions of the male accessory sex organs.
False 2: Androgens regulate the development of the female accessory sex organs.

True Statement: Androgens stimulate muscular growth, growth of facial and axillary hair, aggressiveness, and a low pitch of voice.
False 1: Estrogens stimulate a low pitch of voice.
False 2: Androgens stimulate a high pitch of voice.

True Statement: Androgens play a major stimulatory role in spermatogenesis.
False 1: Estrogens play a major stimulatory role in spermatogenesis.
False 2: Androgens play a major inhibitory role in spermatogenesis.

True Statement: Androgens act on the central neural system and influence male sexual behaviour (libido).
False 1: Estrogens act on the central neural system and influence male sexual behaviour.

True Statement: The ovary produces one ovum during each menstrual cycle.
False 1: The ovary produces two ova during each menstrual cycle.

True Statement: Estrogen is synthesised and secreted mainly by the growing ovarian follicles; after ovulation, the ruptured follicle (corpus luteum) secretes mainly progesterone.
False 1: Progesterone is secreted by the growing ovarian follicles; after ovulation, the corpus luteum secretes mainly estrogen.
False 2: After ovulation, the intact graafian follicle is converted to corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone.

True Statement: Estrogens stimulate growth and activities of female secondary sex organs, development of ovarian follicles, female secondary sex characters (high pitch of voice), and mammary gland development.
False 1: Progesterone stimulates growth and activities of female secondary sex organs and female secondary sex characters.
False 2: Estrogens cause a low pitch of voice in females.

True Statement: Progesterone supports pregnancy and stimulates formation of alveoli and milk secretion from mammary glands.
False 1: Estrogen supports pregnancy and stimulates formation of alveoli and milk secretion.
False 2: Progesterone inhibits milk secretion from mammary glands.

True Statement: The atrial wall of the heart secretes a peptide hormone called atrial natriuretic factor (ANF), which decreases blood pressure.
False 1: The ventricular wall of the heart secretes ANF, which decreases blood pressure.
False 2: ANF increases blood pressure.
False 3: The juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney secrete ANF, which decreases blood pressure.

True Statement: When blood pressure is increased, ANF is secreted, which causes dilation of blood vessels and thereby reduces blood pressure.
False 1: When blood pressure is decreased, ANF is secreted to raise blood pressure.
False 2: ANF causes constriction of blood vessels to reduce blood pressure.

True Statement: The juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney produce a peptide hormone called erythropoietin which stimulates erythropoiesis (formation of RBC).
False 1: The interstitial cells of the kidney produce erythropoietin which stimulates erythropoiesis.
False 2: Juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney produce ANF which stimulates erythropoiesis.
False 3: Erythropoietin produced by kidney inhibits erythropoiesis.

True Statement: The GI tract secretes four major peptide hormones: gastrin, secretin, cholecystokinin (CCK) and gastric inhibitory peptide (GIP).
False 1: The GI tract secretes three major peptide hormones: gastrin, secretin and CCK.

True Statement: Gastrin acts on gastric glands and stimulates secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen.
False 1: Secretin acts on gastric glands and stimulates secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen.
False 2: Gastrin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates secretion of water and bicarbonate ions.

True Statement: Secretin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates secretion of water and bicarbonate ions.
False 1: Gastrin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates secretion of water and bicarbonate ions.
False 2: Secretin acts on the gall bladder and stimulates secretion of water and bicarbonate ions.

True Statement: CCK acts on both pancreas and gall bladder, stimulating secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice respectively.
False 1: Secretin acts on both pancreas and gall bladder, stimulating secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice.
False 2: CCK acts on the gastric glands and stimulates secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen.

True Statement: GIP inhibits gastric secretion and motility.
False 1: Gastrin inhibits gastric secretion and motility.
False 2: GIP stimulates gastric secretion and motility.

True Statement: Hormones produce their effects on target tissues by binding to specific proteins called hormone receptors located in the target tissues only.
False 1: Hormones produce their effects by binding to non-specific proteins located in all tissues.

True Statement: Membrane-bound receptors are present on the cell membrane of target cells; intracellular receptors (mostly nuclear receptors) are present inside the target cell.
False 1: Membrane-bound receptors are present in the nucleus; nuclear receptors are present on the cell membrane.

True Statement: Each receptor is specific to one hormone only.
False 1: Each receptor can bind to multiple hormones.

True Statement: Hormones can be classified as peptide/polypeptide/protein hormones (e.g., insulin, glucagon), steroids (e.g., cortisol, testosterone, estradiol, progesterone), iodothyronines, and amino-acid derivatives (e.g., epinephrine).
False 1: Cortisol is classified as a peptide hormone.
False 2: Insulin is classified as a steroid hormone.

True Statement: Hormones interacting with membrane-bound receptors do not enter the target cell but generate second messengers (e.g., cyclic AMP, IP₃, Ca²⁺) which regulate cellular metabolism.
False 1: Hormones interacting with membrane-bound receptors enter the target cell directly.
False 2: Hormones interacting with intracellular receptors generate second messengers to regulate cellular metabolism.

True Statement: Hormones interacting with intracellular receptors (e.g., steroids, iodothyronines) regulate gene expression or chromosome function by interaction of the hormone-receptor complex with the genome.
False 1: Hormones interacting with membrane-bound receptors regulate gene expression by interaction of hormone-receptor complex with the genome.
False 2: Hormones interacting with intracellular receptors generate second messengers to regulate cellular metabolism.
